learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the division of labor in biology! Learn how identical cells team up to form tissues, creating the complex structures of plants and animals.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A tissue is a group of cells that are similar in structure and work together to achieve a specific function. Just like players on a sports team have different roles, different tissues do different jobs.
Plants have two main types: Meristematic (cells that constantly divide to make the plant grow taller/wider) and Permanent (mature cells that have stopped dividing and taken on a specific job).
These are the plant's plumbing system! Xylem transports water and minerals UP from the roots. Phloem transports food (sugar) from the leaves UP and DOWN to the rest of the plant.

Epithelial tissue covers your body (skin) and lines your organs, acting as a protective barrier. Connective tissue connects and supports the body; surprisingly, Bone, Cartilage, and even liquid BLOOD are all connective tissues!

Muscular tissue is responsible for all movement (voluntary like arms, and involuntary like the heart). Nervous tissue (made of neurons) is your body's electrical wiring, rapidly transmitting messages to and from the brain.

fun_activity.title: 🩸 The Blood Transport Visulaization
fun_activity.instructions: Place a stalk of celery or a white carnation flower in a glass of water dyed with blue or red food coloring. Leave it overnight. The next day, you will see the colored water has travelled up the plant's 'Xylem' tubes to the very top!

exam_tips: 📌 Differentiating between Xylem (Water, one-way flow) and Phloem (Food, two-way flow) is a classic 3-mark question.
📌 Remember the 3 types of muscle tissues: Striated (voluntary), Smooth (involuntary), and Cardiac (heart only, never tires).
📌 Be able to draw and label a Neuron (Nerve cell), pointing out the dendrites, cell body, and axon.
quick_recap: ⭐ The hard shell of a walnut or a coconut husk is made of Sclerenchyma, a dead plant tissue.
⭐ Blood is a unique fluid connective tissue because it transports gases, nutrients, and waste throughout the body.
⭐ Meristematic tissues are found at the growing tips of roots and stems.
